configuration: Full hybrid-triggered Task-oriented Agent with task-state/reminder tracking, in the Qwen3-32B-Finetuned ChronosBench configuration: Qwen3-32B fine-tuned offline by the authors with LoRA (rank 32, 3 epochs, ~2 h on 2 A100s) on 1,052 synthetic dialogs, then evaluated with weights fixed against a GPT-4.1 user simulator on the 216-case ChronosBench test set (temperature 0.2), using the structured-JSON agent prompt of Appendix D.1 (proactive_action, trigger_condition, task_description with status), a simulated backend environment monitor that injects observation messages during user dormancy, and the reminder/task-state tracker described in Sections 3.2, 3.4 and 3.6.
sources_read: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.09382v1 (paper, version 2601.09382v1; Abstract, Sections 1, 2, 3.1-3.6, 4.1-4.3, Limitations, Conclusion, Appendices C, D.1, D.2, E, G, H, Figures 1-2, Tables 1-3) - read through the WebFetch tool's markdown conversion with model-mediated extraction; raw HTML could not be opened in this session (Bash denied), so every quote below is labelled UNVERIFIED even where two independent extractions agreed word for word
No code repository listed in cases/long-term-toa/case.yaml; judged from the text alone

S->M.label: reported
S->M.rationale: User-supplied evidence (initial query Q_t, supplementary constraints C, intention shifts S) and sensed environment state E_t are integrated by the agent into the retained task description T_t = {T_d, T_c, T_s} and reminder M_t each turn; user expressions of satisfaction or refusal are written into the retained status field (COMPLETED/FAILED). Appendix E Listing 1 shows constraints from user turns 5 and 11 being admitted into task_description.constraints and a new trigger_condition.
S->M.locator: Section 3.1.1 (T_t = g(H_t, Q_t, C, S); M_t = h(H_t, Q_t, C, S, E_t)); Section 3.6; Appendix D.1 status rules; Appendix E Listing 1 turns 5-6 and 11-12
S->M.quote: UNVERIFIED: "Upon receiving a initial user inquiry Q_t, the agent must initialize the task description T_t and continuously update it with subsequent supplementary constraints C and intention shifts S" (Section 3.1.1); "When user explicitly expresses that their needs have been met (perhaps express gratitude), the status should be 'COMPLETED'." (Section 3.6)

M->A.label: reported
M->A.rationale: Retained information drives action selection: responses are a function of dialog history H_t (R_t = f(H_t, Q_t, E_t)); at wake-up the observation message carries the original task context alongside the new environment state, and the agent decides FOLLOW_UP vs KEEP_SILENT by checking the new state against the retained constraints; the retained status rule (IN_PROGRESS once a reminder exists) also conditions what the agent outputs.
M->A.locator: Section 3.1 (R_t = f(H_t, Q_t, E_t)); Section 3.1.2; Section 3.2 observation message; Appendix D.1 FOLLOW_UP / KEEP_SILENT instructions; Appendix E Listing 1 turns 9-10 and 15-16
M->A.quote: UNVERIFIED: "the system constructs an observation message to replace the typical user query, and the message contains the updated environment state E_t as well as the original task context." (Section 3.2); "When you receive an <observation> message (triggered by the system, usually containing '**internal trigger**') indicating new info, you should evaluate if it meets the user's needs." (Appendix D.1)

A->S.label: reported
A->S.rationale: Action's information needs and plans direct acquisition in-system: the INFO_RETRIEVAL action triggers a real-time retrieval of E_t whose result returns as an observation message (ReAct-style), and SET_REMINDER formulates a trigger condition (type TIME/EVENT, value) that the backend monitor executes as its filter and that puts the task into a 'monitoring' state after which the system notifies the agent via an internal trigger. This is the paper's 'Intent-Conditioned Monitoring' capability.
A->S.locator: Abstract (Intent-Conditioned Monitoring); Section 3.2 (INFO_RETRIEVAL; backend monitor); Appendix D.1 INFO_RETRIEVAL and SET_REMINDER instructions; Appendix E Listing 1 turns 2-3 and 6-9
A->S.quote: UNVERIFIED: "During active dialog sessions, the agent can perform the action INFO_RETRIEVAL to trigger a real-time retrieval of E_t and immediately receive an observation message involving retrieval results like ReAct" (Section 3.2); "This puts the task in a 'monitoring' state. You do not need to keep checking; the system will notify you via an internal trigger." (Appendix D.1)

M->S.label: reported
M->S.rationale: The retained reminder, stored as a task in a database-driven tracker (task's conditions, task status, last interaction time), is what the backend monitor executes as its filter while periodically scanning the environment during dormancy, i.e., a retained prior supplied to Sensing for sampling/attention rather than an answer-time retrieval. Caveats a voter should weigh: the monitor is introduced with 'We assume', benchmark assumption (iii) has the monitoring framework deliver environment status at a fixed frequency, and the tracker/system architecture is explicitly deferred as engineering detail; under the protocol a simulated or fixed-policy realization does not negate the described flow.
M->S.locator: Section 3.2 (backend monitor paragraph); Section 3.4 (assumption (iii); database-driven tracker sentence); Appendix D.1 SET_REMINDER ('monitoring' state); Appendix E observation messages with source environment_monitor and trigger_type EVENT
M->S.quote: UNVERIFIED: "We assume a backend monitor that periodically scans the environment state. This module acts as a filter, executing the logic defined by the agent's previous reminders." (Section 3.2); "setting up a reminder essentially creates a task within a database-driven tracker module, involving data like username, task's conditions, task status, and last interaction time." (Section 3.4)

A->M.label: reported
A->M.rationale: Action outputs are retained for later use: setting a reminder creates a task record in the database-driven tracker (conditions, status, last interaction time); the agent continuously writes its own task_description/status (status IN_PROGRESS encodes that it has set a reminder) and these JSON responses plus its natural-language replies stay in the dialog history that later turns and the wake-up observation ('original task context') draw on. Retention scope described is a single task episode spanning the active, dormant and wake-up periods (days apart on the simulated timeline); no cross-task or cross-user store is described.
A->M.locator: Section 3.4 (tracker sentence; 'communicates with the system back-end internally through the proactive_action field'); Section 3.6; Section 3.2 ('the agent's previous reminders'); Appendix E Listing 1 turns 6, 8, 12, 14
A->M.quote: UNVERIFIED: "The task-oriented agent needs to keep updated with the task process by continuously modifying the 'status' field in the 'task_description' field ('task_description' is stored in JSON format)." (Section 3.6); "the agent communicates with the system back-end internally through the 'proactive_action' field described in Appendix G." (Section 3.4)

record.label: stated
record.rationale: The service keeps records of its own decisions for later use: each reminder it sets becomes a tracked task entry (conditions, status, last interaction time) that the monitor later executes, and the agent's maintained status field records whether it has set a reminder (PENDING vs IN_PROGRESS). These are service-side records used in later turns, not author-only trial logs.
record.locator: Section 3.4 (database-driven tracker sentence); Section 3.6 (status rules); Section 3.2 ('the agent's previous reminders')
record.quote: UNVERIFIED: "setting up a reminder essentially creates a task within a database-driven tracker module, involving data like username, task's conditions, task status, and last interaction time." (Section 3.4); "When at least one reminder has been set and the task is not completed, the status should be 'IN_PROGRESS'." (Section 3.6)

outcome.label: stated
outcome.rationale: Later evidence about the agent's follow-up is obtained and retained: the user's reply after a FOLLOW_UP (gratitude, refusal/disappointment, cancellation, or an intention shift) is written into the retained task status (COMPLETED/FAILED) and dialog history. Appendix E shows the user's reaction at turn 11 and 17 to the agent's follow-ups at turns 10 and 16 being absorbed into task_description.
outcome.locator: Section 3.6; Appendix D.1 (FAILED_TASK rule 'to your response'); Section 3.5; Appendix E Listing 1 turns 10-12 and 16-18
outcome.quote: UNVERIFIED: "When user expresses refusal/disappointment or asks for cancellation of the task, the status should be 'FAILED'." (Section 3.6); "We assume that users may express that their intentions have changed when the agent first proactively provides information that meets their initial requirements." (Section 3.5)

attribution.label: stated
attribution.rationale: The outcome is linked to the decision it concerns and used to correct assistance within the task: refusal/disappointment 'to your response' must be attributed to that response and ends the task as FAILED_TASK, and an intention shift voiced after the agent's first follow-up must lead the agent to set a new reminder with the updated constraints instead of repeating retrieval. This is an immediate, service-side check; the paper's action/status-accuracy scoring is offline author scoring and was not counted.
attribution.locator: Appendix D.1 (FAILED_TASK rule); Section 3.5 (new reminder after intention shift); Section 4.3 failure analysis of agents that fail to re-set reminders
attribution.quote: UNVERIFIED: "Whenever the user expresses refusal/disappointment (do not include constraints supplement and intention shift) to your response, you should set proactive_action to FAILED_TASK." (Appendix D.1); "It's better for the agent to set a new reminder immediately after user describes their intention shift rather than performing yet another redundant information retrieval by 'INFO_RETRIEVAL'." (Section 3.5)

revision.label: not_stated
revision.rationale: No durable change to the mechanism is made by the service. The only parameter change is the authors' offline LoRA supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3-32B on synthetic data before evaluation; the agent prompt (Appendix D.1/D.2) is fixed and authored by the developers; what the agent updates at run time (task_description intention/constraints/status, trigger_condition) is task-state content consumed by a fixed mechanism, not a reusable rule. Learning per-user tolerance thresholds is named only as future work.
revision.locator: Section 4 / 4.2 (fine-tuning hyper-parameters: LoRA rank 32, batch 16, lr 3e-5, 3 epochs, 2 A100s); Appendix D.1-D.2; Limitations item 3 'Definition of Intrusiveness'
revision.quote: UNVERIFIED: "Future work should investigate personalized proactivity thresholds, allowing the agent to learn specific user tolerance levels for interruptions." (Limitations, item 3); "For training Qwen3-32B, we employ LoRA rank of 32, a total batch size of 16, a learning rate of 3e-5, and an AdamW Optimizer with a 0.1 warm-up ratio." (Section 4)
revision.what: Nothing is revised by the service; model weights were changed once by the authors offline (LoRA SFT) and prompts are developer-written.

later_use.label: not_stated
later_use.rationale: Because the service makes no revision, no later step runs under a service-revised mechanism. Evaluation runs use the authors' fine-tuned weights fixed with the user simulator; this is later use of a developer change, which does not count.
later_use.locator: Section 4.2-4.3 evaluation procedure ('The models under test engage in dialogs with the user simulator on the test set and the temperature is set to 0.2'); Conclusion

notes: Judged the Qwen3-32B-Finetuned ChronosBench configuration of the hybrid-triggered task-oriented agent (Sections 3.2-3.6, Appendix D.1 prompt, 85.19% complex-scene completion in Table 3). Memory in this system is the per-task retained state: dialog history H_t, the agent-maintained task_description JSON, and the reminder/trigger_condition stored as a task in a database-driven tracker; retention spans the active, dormant and wake-up periods of one task episode (observation timestamps in Appendix E are weeks apart) but no cross-task or cross-user memory is described, and the tracker/system architecture is explicitly left as 'engineering implementation methods'. The basic S->A path (user query and observation messages reaching the agent) was not reviewed. Only text sources were available; the arXiv HTML was read through the WebFetch tool's markdown conversion with model-mediated extraction because shell access was denied, so all quotes are marked UNVERIFIED even though independent extractions returned identical wording. The case-file sha256 for the HTML could not be checked for the same reason.
